question: The substances that are used for making food products unsafe for human consumption are known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**adulterants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Adulterants** are substances that are intentionally added to food products to reduce their quality, increase quantity, or make them unsafe for consumption. This is often done for economic benefits.
 
• Adulterants can be harmful to human health and may cause short-term illnesses (like food poisoning) or long-term diseases (such as cancer, organ damage, etc.).
 
• Common examples of adulterants include **chalk powder in flour, washing powder in milk, artificial dyes in spices**, and others.
 
• Adulteration is considered a violation of food safety standards and is strictly regulated under food safety laws such as the **Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 in India**.
 
• Unlike food additives, which are approved substances used to enhance food properties, adulterants are illegal and harmful.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Food Additives:**

 
 
• Food additives are substances added to food to preserve flavor, enhance taste, or improve shelf life.
 
• Examples include **preservatives (like sodium benzoate), emulsifiers, colorants, and flavor enhancers (like monosodium glutamate - MSG)**.
 
• They are regulated by food safety authorities and are safe for consumption when used within prescribed limits.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Hazards:**
 
 
• These refer to the harmful chemicals present in food due to contamination or improper handling, such as pesticides, heavy metals, or industrial chemicals.
 
• Unlike adulterants, chemical hazards are usually unintentional.
 
• For example, **arsenic in water or pesticide residues on vegetables** can pose serious health risks.
 
 
 
• **Flavouring Agents:**
 
 
• Flavouring agents are substances added to food to enhance or modify its taste and aroma.
 
• They are widely used in processed foods and beverages, such as **vanilla extract, citric acid, or artificial fruit flavors**.
 
• Approved flavoring agents are generally safe and regulated by food safety authorities.
 
 
 
• **Food Adulteration Laws:**
 
 
• In India, food adulteration is regulated by the **Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)** under the **Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006**.
 
• Severe penalties, including fines and imprisonment, are imposed on individuals or entities found guilty of adulteration.
 
• Awareness campaigns like **"Jaago Grahak Jaago"** educate consumers about food safety and adulteration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Health Risks of Adulteration:**

 
 
• Adulterants like **metanil yellow in turmeric** can cause liver damage and cancer.
 
• Contaminated milk with **detergents** can lead to gastrointestinal disorders.
 
• Chalk powder or starch in flour can impair digestion.
 
 
 
• **Detection of Adulterants:**
 
 
• Simple home tests, such as the "water test" for milk adulteration or iodine test for starch in sugar, can help detect common adulterants.
 
• Advanced lab techniques, like chromatography and spectroscopy, are used for precise detection of adulterants.
 
 
 
• **Preventive Measures:**
 
 
• Consumers should purchase food products from trusted sources and check for **FSSAI certification**.
 
• Awareness campaigns and stricter enforcement of food safety regulations can curb adulteration practices.
